idea.body: A triangle's midsegment joins the midpoints of two sides. It runs parallel to the third side and is exactly half its length. A drone frame with sides 12, 16 and 20 centimeters has a midsegment of length 6, cutting across parallel to the 12 centimeter side. The three medians of a triangle, each from one vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, always cross at one point called the centroid. It splits every median in a 2 to 1 ratio from the vertex. A 15 centimeter median becomes a 10 centimeter piece and a 5 centimeter piece. Triangles also follow size rules. Two sides always add to more than the third side, and the longest side always sits across from the largest angle.

figure.alt: A triangle with sides 16, 12 and 20. A dashed midsegment of length 6 joins the midpoints of the sides of length 16 and 20, parallel to the side of length 12.

workedExample.prompt: A rover's frame is a triangle. One of its medians is 18 centimeters long. The centroid splits every median in a 2 to 1 ratio from the vertex. Find the distance from the vertex to the centroid.
steps: The centroid splits a median into two pieces in a 2 to 1 ratio, the longer piece next to the vertex.
The two pieces together make the whole median, so they are 2 parts and 1 part of 3 total parts.
Each part is 18 divided by 3, which is 6 centimeters.
The vertex to centroid piece is 2 parts, so it is 2 times 6, which is 12 centimeters.

figure.alt: A triangle with a median from the top vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, and the centroid G marked on that median.

ways.name: The midsegment is half the base
ways.when: Use this when a segment joins the midpoints of two sides of a triangle.
steps: A ramp brace is a right triangle with legs 8 and 15 centimeters and hypotenuse 17 centimeters.
A midsegment joins the midpoints of two sides and runs parallel to the third side.
It is always exactly half as long as that third side.
The midsegment here is parallel to the 8 centimeter leg.
Half of 8 is 4, so the midsegment is 4 centimeters.
ways.example: A right triangle has legs 8 and 15 centimeters. Find the midsegment parallel to the 8 centimeter leg.
ways.trap: Taking half of the hypotenuse instead of half of the side the midsegment runs parallel to.

figure.alt: A right triangle with legs 8 and 15 centimeters and hypotenuse 17 centimeters. A dashed midsegment joins the midpoints of the two legs.

frames.caption: It's half the length of the third side

ways.name: The centroid splits a median 2 to 1
ways.when: Use this when you know a median's full length and want the piece near the vertex.
steps: A frame's median from a vertex to the opposite side's midpoint is 21 centimeters long.
The centroid splits every median into a 2 to 1 ratio, the longer piece next to the vertex.
The two pieces make 3 equal parts total, so each part is 21 divided by 3, which is 7.
The vertex to centroid piece is 2 parts, so it is 2 times 7, which is 14 centimeters.
ways.example: A triangle's median is 21 centimeters long. Find the distance from the vertex to the centroid.
ways.trap: Splitting the median into two equal halves instead of a 2 to 1 ratio.

ways.name: The longest side faces the largest angle
ways.when: Use this when you know a triangle's angles and want to order its sides by length.
steps: A triangle has angles 40, 65 and 75 degrees, with sides a, b, c across from them in that order.
The largest angle is always across from the longest side.
The smallest angle is always across from the shortest side.
75 degrees is the largest angle and 40 degrees is the smallest.
So side c is the longest side and side a is the shortest side.
ways.example: A triangle has angles 40, 65 and 75 degrees, with sides a, b, c across from them. Order the sides by length.
ways.answer: c is longest, then b, then a is shortest
ways.trap: Matching a side to the angle next to it instead of the angle directly across from it.

frames.caption: Triangle: angles 40, 65, 75; sides a, b, c.
Angles 40, 65, 75; sides a, b, c opposite
Largest angle faces the longest side
Smallest angle faces the shortest side
So c is longest, a is shortest

ways.name: The two shorter sides must beat the third
ways.when: Use this to check whether three given lengths can actually form a triangle.
steps: Three rods measure 5, 7 and 13 centimeters.
Add the two shortest lengths: 5 plus 7 is 12.
Compare that sum to the longest side: 12 is less than 13.
Since the sum is not greater than the third side, the rods cannot form a triangle.
ways.example: Can rods of 5, 7 and 13 centimeters form a triangle?
ways.trap: Adding any two sides instead of the two shortest, which is the tightest case to check.

bank.prompt: Put these steps of a proof in order to show that in triangle ABC, AB + BC is greater than AC.
items: Triangle BDC is isosceles, so angle BDC equals angle BCD.
Angle ACD is angle ACB plus angle BCD, so angle ACD is greater than angle BDC.
In triangle ACD, the side opposite the larger angle is longer, so AD is greater than AC.
Since AD equals AB plus BD, and BD equals BC, AB plus BC is greater than AC.
Extend side AB beyond B to a point D so that BD = BC.
explanation: The proof builds a bigger triangle, ACD, by extending a side.
It compares angles in that bigger triangle first, then converts the angle comparison into a side comparison.
The last step swaps BD back for BC to reach the triangle inequality.
hints: The construction step, extending a side, always comes first.
The angle comparison comes before the side comparison it leads to.
bank.socraticHint: What has to be built before any angle in triangle ACD can be compared?

stretch.prompt: Triangle ABC has AB = 13, BC = 14 and CA = 15. Let M be the midpoint of BC. What is AM squared?
explanation: The median length formula gives AM squared as (2 times CA squared, plus 2 times AB squared, minus BC squared) all over 4.
That is (2 times 225 plus 2 times 169 minus 196) over 4.
450 plus 338 minus 196 is 592, and 592 over 4 is 148.
hints: Use the median length formula rather than trying to guess a whole number median.
AM itself is not a whole number, which is why the problem asks for AM squared.
